title: How Many, and At What
scopeNote: This keeps the participation model, the target weighting, the concentration measure and the disinhibition index, with the five independent conditions reduced to four scenarios and one live control. Setting each condition separately and the exercise on what would falsify each account are in the longer version.
summary: Four fictional afternoons and one toggle. Two of them score identically on the measure an account of lost restraint tracks, and their concentration figures are 0.12 and 0.76.
learningObjectives: Say how the two accounts differ about the patterning of crowd action.
Say where each locates the cause.
Explain why a measure of how many joined in cannot distinguish two very different afternoons.
Explain why anonymity sharpens the action where a shared understanding exists and broadens it where none does.
Recognise that each account is right about the direction in some conditions.
interactionTypes: a judgement about which account a concentrated pattern fits
four scenarios chosen one at a time
a live identifiability toggle whose direction of effect depends on the scenario
a target-share figure and a section-by-section participation table
a computed matched pair of afternoons with identical indices
privacy: Nothing is collected, stored or transmitted.
dataStatus: A fictional town and a fictional afternoon. Every number comes from a teaching model whose rules are printed on the page, and no event, police operation or town described here is real.
accessibilityNotes: Keyboard operable throughout. The scenario is a group of native radio buttons in a labelled fieldset, and identifiability is a button carrying aria-pressed with a visible word saying which state it is in. Every target's share is labelled in words on its bar as well as being given in the chart description, and the section-by-section participation is a real table with row and column headers whose verdict column reads yes or no. The matched pair is a table, not a figure. Nothing is timed and there is no motion.
simulationNotes: A section takes part when its baseline readiness plus unity times legitimacy, plus a norm shift if it is inside the common category, reaches the threshold. Target weights are set by the norm and then reshaped by identifiability, and that reshaping is where the two accounts part company: where a shared norm is in play anonymity sharpens it, with each weight raised to a power above one and renormalised, and where there is no shared understanding anonymity moves the weights part of the way towards an even spread instead. The consequence, verified across all four scenarios in the test suite, is that anonymity raises concentration in the two afternoons with a shared understanding and lowers it in the two without, so each account is right about the direction in half the cases and neither is a straw man. The disinhibition index is identifiability together with how many sections joined in, which is what an account of lost restraint tracks, and it is printed so that two afternoons can be seen scoring the same on it. The guided comparison finds that pair by searching all eight runs for the two with identical indices and the largest difference in concentration; it is computed rather than written down, and the test suite verifies that the indices are exactly equal, that the section counts match, and that the concentrations differ by more than half the scale. The concentration measure is the summed absolute deviation of the four shares from an even quarter, scaled so that zero is an even spread and one is everything on a single target. It is a teaching device invented for this page and not a published statistic.
readmeTopic: why two theories of crowd action disagree about shape rather than about amount
